newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS TECHNICAL CHIEF TO FIGHT TO CLEAR NAME.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS TECHNICAL CHIEF TO FIGHT TO CLEAR NAME.

text.p: Williams technical director Patrick Head said on Thursday he will fight as strongly as possible to clear his name when he faces magistrates in the Ayrton Senna case in Imola.

Head, along with Williams team chief Frank Williams and chief designer Adrian Newey, has been charged with manslaughter following the death of Ayrton Senna at the San Marino Grand Prix on May 1, 1994.

Head and Williams confirmed on Thursday they will not be present at the opening day of the trial on February 20, but Head said that whatever the outcome of the case he would pursue it in order to keep his record as an engineer clear of any charges.

He said: "It is a very serious matter, a criminal case, and we are therefore taking it very seriously. For myself as an engineer it is something I do not want to have on my record and I am prepared, if the case goes against us, to appeal and fight on for as long as necessary to clear my name."
Head said it was "not ideal" to be working with the impending trial hovering like a cloud over the team as they prepared for the new Formula One season.
Speaking at an informal lunch with British reporters, Head also echoed Williams' prediction that the 1997 Formula One season would be much closer and much tougher than it was for the team last year.
Williams said: "It is going to be much harder, very much harder. I know it will be."

Head said he did not have a "rosy feeling" about the team's prospects, but agreed he did not have such feelings 12 months earlier before Briton Damon Hill won the opening four races on his way to claiming last year's world drivers' title.
But he felt the team's Canadian driver Jacques Villeneuve deserved his position as pre-season championship favourite.
"He has all the skills and the race craft and I see no reason why he cannot be very competitive and very successful this year," he said.

Asked about Villeneuve's new team mate, German Heinz-Harald Frentzen, who has succeeded Hill, Head said he thought he would be as fast as the Canadian in qualifying but had a feeling that Villeneuve would prove to be the fastest of the two drivers when it came to the races.
